title: Gang Busters
paragraphs: Phillips H. Lord true-crime dramatization series built from actual law-enforcement cases, wanted-person bulletins and police/federal cooperation.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: G-Men precursor (July 20, 1935 to October 12, 1935) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS Gang Busters launch era (January 15, 1936 to June 15, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Blue Network era (October 11, 1940 to 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], and ABC era (1945 to December 25, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Phillips H. Lord (producer, creator, and executive producer), Stanley Niss (writer and director), Don Gardiner (announcer), William Sweets (director and producer), Leonard L. Bass (director), Frank Readick (performer), and Gaylord Avery (announcer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]], [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]].
The stories often return to organized criminal gangs, robbery and burglary, murder and homicide, wanted fugitives, prisons and escapes, and law enforcement investigation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes True-crime radio and public confidence in law enforcement, Citizen-detective wanted-person bulletins, Gang Busters sound-effects opening and popular phrase, and 1930s gangster and G-man popular culture.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]], and [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]].
